{
  "description": "World Monitor is a real-time global intelligence dashboard and OSINT platform focused on news aggregation, geopolitical monitoring, and infrastructure tracking. It provides situational awareness interfaces via web apps, CLI, and SDKs across multiple languages (TypeScript, Python, Ruby, Go). The system utilizes Convex for backend data persistence and state management, with various specialized Dockerfiles for different deployment variants (e.g., digest notifications, relay, seed bundles).",

      "evidence_refs": [
        "api/oref-alerts.js@fefc3e7b",
        "convex/alertRules.ts@fefc3e7b"
      ],
      "notes": "The repository contains alert-related infrastructure including an 'oref' (likely OpenRef or similar) alerts relay endpoint and Convex-based alert rule management with sensitivity levels ('high', 'critical'). However, it lacks explicit emergency-specific handling logic (e.g., priority queuing, broadcast mechanisms) in the sampled code. It appears to be a general-purpose alerting system rather than a dedicated emergency service."
    },

    "Docker"

  "deployment_constraints": [
    "Requires Convex account/backend for state management and alert rules",
    "Multi-stage Docker build requires Rust toolchain and Node.js 24",
    "Edge runtime support (Vercel/Cloudflare likely, given 'runtime: edge' config)"
  ],
  "maturity": "stable",
  "adaptation_hours_estimate": 40,
  "adaptation_confidence": "low",
  "adaptation_assumptions": [
    "The existing alert infrastructure (Convex rules, relay handlers) can be extended to support emergency-specific logic and acknowledgement workflows.",
    "MQTT integration for alerts would require new middleware or adapters not present in the current HTTPS/Convex stack.",
    "Device status monitoring is out of scope and would need significant new development."
  ],
  "known_gaps": [
    "No MQTT support for alert ingestion or dispatch (requested interfaces are MQTT, repo uses HTTPS/Convex)",
    "No explicit emergency alert prioritization or broadcast handling",
    "No alert acknowledgement state management or UI components",
    "No device telemetry or status monitoring capabilities"
  ],
  "risks": [
    "AGPL v3 license requires source disclosure for network use, which may be incompatible with proprietary defense architectures.",
    "Heavy reliance on Convex (third-party BaaS) creates vendor lock-in and potential single point of failure.",
    "Complex multi-stage Docker builds with pinned digests may hinder rapid adaptation or offline deployment."
  ],
  "evidence": [
    {
      "claim": "Repository is a real-time global intelligence dashboard for news and geopolitical monitoring.",

      "verified": true
    },
    {
      "claim": "Uses AGPL v3 license.",

      "verified": true
    }
  ]
